The contrast ratio

ratio = (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05)

  • L1 relative luminance of the lighter color
  • L2 relative luminance of the darker color
  • 0.05 a fixed constant added to both luminances

Browser extension toolkit (install once, used across phases) · 3/7

Two thresholds

Normal text

  • Needs at least 4.5:1
  • Below 18 pt, or below 14 pt bold

Large text

  • Needs at least 3:1
  • 18 pt, or 14 pt bold

Larger text may use lower contrast.

Browser extension toolkit (install once, used across phases) · 7/7

What rules cannot judge

A rule decides

  • Contrast of plain colors
  • A skipped heading level

A person judges

  • Text on an image
  • Heading meaning
  • Keyboard and screen reader use

Zero violations does not mean accessible.

One accessibility scan gives three answers: pass, fail, or incomplete.

Incomplete means the tool cannot decide, so a person must review it.

The contrast ratio compares two colors.

L1 is the relative luminance of the lighter color,

and L2 is the luminance of the darker color.

Normal text needs a ratio of at least 4.5 to 1.

Large text, 18 point or 14 point bold,

needs at least 3 to 1.

Gray 767676 on white scores 4.54 and passes.

Gray 777777 scores 4.47 and fails.

Axe rounds down, so 4.47 never shows as 4.5.

Some cases return incomplete: text on a background image,

an overlapping element, one-character text, or an empty input field.

Heading order checks each heading against the one before it.

After h2, an h4 skips a level and fails.

Change it to h3, and it passes.

A rule decides plain color contrast and skipped heading levels.

A person judges text on images,

heading meaning, and keyboard and screen reader use.
